title: The Day a Protection Plan Is Treated as Given Up From
content:
The day a Pass and Trip Protection plan is treated as given up from, for the purpose of measuring the part of
its term still to come, is settled from what the plan's own record and its claim history show.

1. Where no claim has been made on the plan in the season, no paper stands filed against one and the plan's
   record carries no day on which cover was closed, the plan is treated as given up from the day the household
   gives it up.
2. Where the plan's record carries a day on which cover was closed, the plan is treated as given up from the
   day its record shows cover was closed.
3. In every other case the plan is treated as given up from the day cover began.

**What the first case requires.** All three of its limbs must hold together: no claim made on the plan within
the season, no paper filed against a claim on it, and no day on which cover was closed standing on the plan's
record. One paper filed against a claim is enough to take the plan off the first case.

**Illustrations (hypothetical inputs).** A plan with no claim and no paper against one, and no closing day on
its record: the day taken is the day the household gives it up. A plan whose record already carries a day on
which cover was closed: the day taken is that day, whatever its claim history. A plan carrying a claim made in
the season, or a paper filed against one, and no closing day on its record: the day taken is the day cover
began.
